### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**1** anchor(s) derived from **2** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **178** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 895783a1e864e0fe629c56b3c6315771ca87bf87` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b75c9a32b42b831c5a7e0c78d524fef527ffae98` — the merge of head `f3979189f3e0a90cf559147254dc4d5a4797c8b8` into base `895783a1e864e0fe629c56b3c6315771ca87bf87`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b75c9a32b42b831c5a7e0c78d524fef527ffae98 && git checkout b75c9a32b42b831c5a7e0c78d524fef527ffae98
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 895783a1e864e0fe629c56b3c6315771ca87bf87 f3979189f3e0a90cf559147254dc4d5a4797c8b8 && git checkout -B drift-repro 895783a1e864e0fe629c56b3c6315771ca87bf87 && git merge --no-ff f3979189f3e0a90cf559147254dc4d5a4797c8b8

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 895783a1e864e0fe629c56b3c6315771ca87bf87
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `f3979189f3e0a90cf559147254dc4d5a4797c8b8`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.notify-channel-unknown-refused.ts + packages/runtime/src/domains/automation.ts

### ① Derived judgments

- Spec entry: only `reason` moves. `id`, `surface`, `replacement`, `acceptanceCriteria` are byte-identical; no `conversionIds`, no `relevantWhen`. Right: prose only, no machine-read field.
- No generated artifact is owed. `reason` is read by `os migrate meta` (`cli/src/commands/migrate/meta.ts` printNotice) and by `build-upgrade-guide.ts` ("Why not automatic"), which generates in memory on a PR and writes at publish or docs build; `docs/protocol-upgrade-guide.md` is a pointer stub, no `spec-changes.json` is committed, and no test pins this entry's text.
- Runtime door: the accepted set grows in one case only, a `getKnownChannels()` list with a member off `{ id: string }`. A list of well-shaped members, the empty list included, is judged exactly as on main. Nothing accepted on main is refused at the head. Right.
- Check-runs at review time: 13 success, 10 skipped, 21 in progress, 0 failed. Unconcluded: Test Core 1-8, both builds, Live E2E UI, Type Check and most Lint jobs. This record judges the contract and does not vouch for those verdicts.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on `@objectstack/runtime` (a bug fix) and on `@objectstack/spec` (published data text) is right; `Metadata-protocol: none` is right, no authorable key or value moves.

Clause-②: no. It holds. The one case that moves from 400 to 200 is reachable only through a messaging service that breaks the reader contract the check declares (`NotifyChannelRegistry`; its one producer `MessagingService.getKnownChannels()` answers the declared shape). The released 18.4 text already says an unreadable reader is not judged; the change makes that true for a third unreadable form. No declared composition changes its answer, so it is not a widening of the accept set, and it is not a narrowing: the head accepts a superset of main. Had it been ruled `yes (widening)`, the level would still be `patch`.

Changeset sentences read against the head: true, with one overstatement, N1 below.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty.
- Declined N3: accepted. `relevantWhen` is to be omitted unless the surface lives only under top-level stack keys (`migrations/types.ts`); this surface is a flow saved through the runtime `/automation` doors, so no stack question can prove it absent. The card made N3 optional and conditional.
- Out-of-scope note with no carrier: `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx` still names only `nodes.N.config.channels` and one not-judged case. The card's N2 asked the entry to agree with it; the entry now says more than the page. See N2.
- The fail-open is the card's own instruction: with a malformed roster an unknown channel also saves. The run-time failure is unchanged; the door guards authoring quality, not access.

### ④ Design judgment

Entry `reason`, sentence by sentence against `refuseUnknownNotifyChannels` at the head:
- Paths: `field` is graph.path + nodes.N.config.channels + the member index; `collectFlowGraphs` prefixes a region with nodes.I.config.SLOT. True for all three forms.
- Did-you-mean and roster: `nearestName` and the `roster` line. True.
- "reader throws, answers no list, or a list with a member that is not a channel": the catch, the `Array.isArray` return and the new `every(isChannel)` return. True.
- "a save before kernel:ready has settled": `isRequestKernelReady` is `hasBootPhaseSettled('kernel:ready')` in `http-dispatcher.ts`. True.
- Package flow, metadata door, boot row: unchanged text, still true.

`automation.ts`: the guard, the jsdoc bullet and the inline comment agree with each other and with the entry. Tried to break it: a Promise from an async reader, `null` members, `[]`, a member with `id` and no `configured`; each lands where the text says.

Test pin (lane ACCEPT): both shapes save 200 naming `email`; under the old filter both rosters lack `email`, so the reported ablation failure (expected 400 to be 200) is the right one.

No must-fix, no should-fix.

- N1 nit: the changeset says the entry "lists every not-judged case". A messaging service with no `getKnownChannels()` is a not-judged case the function's jsdoc names; the entry and the released changelog do not. No entry sentence is false. Accepted deviation.
- N2 nit: file a docs card for `flows.mdx`.
